lessons.title: Stock records and the stock balance
lessons.html:
Why stock control matters

At a grain silo, stock is the grain in bins, bunkers and sheds, held for farmers, traders and the company. Much of it is not the silo's own grain; it is held on behalf of depositors who have silo receipts or certificates. The silo must be able to show, at any time, how much of each commodity and grade it holds and for whom. Losses mean money, and missing stock can mean legal claims.

The basic stock equation

Closing stock = Opening stock + Receipts - Dispatches +/- Adjustments

Adjustments include drying shrinkage, cleaning losses, re-grading and approved write-offs. Every adjustment needs a reason and an authorisation.

Source documents

  • Weighbridge tickets for every truck in and out: gross, tare and nett mass.
  • Grading certificates giving grade, moisture and deductions.
  • Bin cards or bin registers showing which grain went into or out of each bin.
  • Transfer documents for grain moved between bins or sites.
  • Receipts and release orders showing ownership and authority to dispatch.

Keeping records accurate

  • Record every movement on the day it happens.
  • Number documents in sequence and account for every number, including cancelled ones.
  • Reconcile the weighbridge total with the stock system daily.
  • Keep each commodity and grade separate in the records, just as it is physically separate in the bins.
  • Check that the person who weighs is not the only person who records and approves. Separating duties reduces fraud.

Example

Bin 4 opened the week with 1 850 t of white maize grade 1. Receipts were 620 t and dispatches 400 t. Drying shrinkage of 12 t was approved. Book closing stock is 1 850 + 620 - 400 - 12 = 2 058 t.

lessons.title: Stock counts, variances and preventing losses
lessons.html:
Stock counts and variances

Physical stock counts

Book stock must be checked against what is physically there. In bulk grain this is done by measuring the grain level in bins and calculating volume, then converting to mass using the bin's measurements and the bulk density of the grain (hectolitre mass). Bag stock is counted by stacks.

  • Plan the count: date, bins, team, equipment.
  • Stop or record all movements during the count.
  • Use calibrated tapes or level sensors and the official bin tables.
  • Two people take and sign each reading.
  • Follow confined space and working-at-heights rules on bin roofs.

Variances

A variance is the difference between book stock and physical stock. Small variances are expected because bulk measurement is not exact and grain loses moisture. Large variances must be investigated.

Possible causeWhat to check
Recording errorsMissing or duplicated tickets, wrong bin numbers
Weighbridge errorCalibration certificate, test weights
Moisture loss or gainMoisture at intake versus now
Spillage or pestsConveyor leaks, rodent and bird activity
TheftSecurity records, unauthorised dispatches

Report variances to management with the cause found and the corrective action. Adjustments are only made with authorisation.

Preventing losses

  • Keep grain cool and dry and monitor bin temperatures to prevent spoilage.
  • Run an integrated pest control programme and fumigate only through registered operators following Act 36 of 1947 product labels.
  • Fix conveyor and spout leaks and clean spills.
  • Control access to bins, weighbridge and dispatch.
  • Rotate stock: first in, first out where ownership allows.

Reporting

Produce regular stock reports by commodity, grade, owner and bin. Show opening stock, movements, closing stock, variances and stock condition. Management uses these to plan dispatch, storage space and sales.

Key points

  • Closing stock equals opening stock plus receipts minus dispatches, plus or minus authorised adjustments.
  • Every movement needs a source document recorded the same day.
  • Compare book stock with physical counts and investigate large variances.
  • Separate duties and control access to prevent fraud and theft.
  • Prevent losses with good storage, pest control and leak repair.
